label: input x at original position 1 or 2
explanation: Fires whenever the input token is x at step t=1 or t=2 of the original phase, with no other conditions: every such step is active (precision 1.0), and nearly all activations are covered. Magnitude depends on position: about 0.95-1.0 of max at t=1 (71% of mass) and about 0.3-0.45 at t=2. Preceding tokens, L and first token have little effect on magnitude. It does not fire on x at t=0 or t>=3, on any other token, at the delimiter, or in the copy phase, except for 8 tiny copy-phase activations (<0.3) where x is fed back as an input.

issues: No systematic counterexamples found. On the test split there are 0 false positives and 4 misses holding 0.0% of activation mass (three are tiny copy-phase x at step 17, one is a 0.04 echo at step 5). Test F1 is 0.99994 and mass recall is 0.99998. The reported 1.000 is rounding.

The phase and position claims check out. Activations at t=0, at t>=3 in the original phase, and at the delimiter are all 0. The copy phase has 8/33359 dev activations, all small. Every activation is on in_tok x. Mass split is t=1 0.709 and t=2 0.291.

Small imprecision in the magnitude claim: t=2 activations go as low as about 0.28 of max (e.g. 'g o [x:0.28] h'), not only 0.3-0.45. Also, a large first-token effect cannot be ruled out from the first_tok breakdown alone, but the t=1 examples cluster tightly at 0.95-1.00 regardless of first token, so this is minor.
